results.summary_before: This SystemVerilog design performs grayscale conversion, Sobel edge detection, and thresholding on pixel data received over an SPI interface. Processing modes are selected via input pins, and an internal LFSR can optionally supply test pixels instead of external SPI data. The design requires an external SPI master such as a Raspberry Pi to send pixel data, and the processed result appears on a single output pin. The documentation is brief but includes a block diagram and pin-level usage details, though the thresholding and LFSR behavior are only lightly described.

results.summary_before: TRI-1 Gamma is a 32-tile neuromorphic design combining eight cortical columns with leaky-integrate-and-fire dynamics and ternary MLP layers, a 20-PE GF16 mesh, and 24 supporting modules including ROMs, matrix multipliers, a Blake3 anchor and monitors. It includes a four-port die-to-die router for multi-chip spike propagation, and on reset it drives the canonical constant 0x47C0 onto the output pins. The design uses a custom GF16 floating-point format with shift-and-add mantissa multiplication, and no external hardware is required for single-die testing. The documentation is dense and uses unusual terminology, so the exact function of many blocks is hard to verify from the text alone.
